resources.string: Control other devices with the keyboard and mouse connected to this device

KeymaHub receives input from the keyboard and mouse connected to this device and sends it to the Bluetooth device (PC, tablet) you choose with a hotkey. When this device is selected, input is left as it is. Input is never stored or sent to the internet; it only goes to the device you choose. KeymaHub does not read screen content, except a text field you touch on this device while another device is controlled: its text is read so you can type into it with the on-screen keyboard.
Use the keyboard and mouse connected to this device to control PCs and tablets nearby. Nothing needs to be installed on them.
This device connects to your devices as a Bluetooth keyboard and mouse.

How KeymaHub uses the accessibility service
KeymaHub uses the accessibility service only to:
• Receive input from the keyboard and mouse connected to this device.
• Send that input to the Bluetooth device (PC, tablet) you select with a hotkey. While this device is selected, input is left as it is.
• Input is never stored and never sent to the internet or to the developer. It only goes to the device you select.
• KeymaHub does not read screen content, except a text field you touch on this device while another device is controlled: its text is read so you can type into it with the on-screen keyboard.

How input is sent over Bluetooth. Changes apply at once. If unsure, keep the recommended values.

The shortest time between two mouse movement reports sent to the device. Movement in between is added up and sent as one. Lower is smoother but sends more; if the Bluetooth link cannot keep up, reports pile up and the mouse lags. Higher lags less but moves less smoothly. If the mouse lags, raise it (e.g. 12–16); if it feels choppy, lower it.

How many reports may be handed to the Bluetooth stack before it confirms them. Reports in the stack can no longer be merged, so more of them means more lag when the link is slow. Fewer means less lag, but less is sent at a time and motion may look choppy.

How long to wait for the stack to confirm sent reports before counting them as lost and sending on. Too short, and a slow link\'s normal confirmations count as lost, so more is pushed into the stack (a cause of lag). Too long, and sending pauses that long when a confirmation really is lost. If the log often shows \'unconfirmed after\', raise it.
How soon a report the Bluetooth stack was too busy for is tried again. Shorter retries sooner but uses a little more CPU.
Input that waits this long or longer is written to the app log (\'waited … ms\'). For diagnosis only: it does not change sending.

Asks devices for Bluetooth LE 2M. Each packet takes half the air time, leaving more room for other devices and Wi-Fi. The device decides whether to use it. Far away or with heavy interference, off may be steadier. A change is requested from connected devices at once.
Takes this phone\'s mouse movement as it comes, instead of once per screen frame (8–16 ms). On reacts faster; off handles fewer events. Android 11 and later.
